terra.problem: Paul's status as an apostle and his audience in Ephesus come from Ephesians 1:1, and his chains from Ephesians 6:20. Those facts need references. The passage also does not say this was the first thing on his mind.
Paul says they were called to one hope; he does not state that there is a single calling.
The verse says they were called to one hope, not explicitly that there is one shared calling.
The verse says God is over all, through all and in all. Saying there is no spot He is missing from turns that into a claim about every location.
It assumes the individual baker is included in Paul's statement about grace, though Papa Dorin has not been told about the baker's faith.
The verse gives filling all things as the purpose of the ascent. It does not say filling is the opposite of leaving, or frame the ascent as the opposite of leaving things behind.
The explanation is a flat restatement: rest is not in the verse, but filling is. It has no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The definitions of apostles and prophets bring in Bible facts beyond this passage without references.
The claim that kings and priests are roles in the Bible brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Calling these four kinds of people settles whether pastors and teachers are one kind, which the wording leaves open.
The claim that judges and elders are roles elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
The explanation repeats the verse and says it is in verse 12, without adding a distinctive voice or insight.

Saying Paul says the opposite implies that every wind of teaching is harmful. He warns against being carried around by every wind and mentions deceitful scheming, but does not say that every teaching is harmful.
The cookie-with-no-dough comparison does not make sense as an image, and the punchline does not clarify the connection between truth and love.
Saying love is how the words are spoken 'whatever the words are' leaves out Paul's instruction to speak the truth.
The passage says the body grows through the work of each part. It does not say that the body feels it if one part is missing.
